rel_notes.n: Fixes: the two benchmark pages have distinct names in every language, market variants of cost databases are listed for every role with install kept to editors, stale resource changes are refused, and generated design texts follow the interface language.

The data paths panel on every module page now opens on a plain-words overview: where the numbers come from, what the module holds right now, who uses them next, and which gaps break what.

### Added

- Data paths overview tab: a three-step story with live counts and amounts, a health strip naming each empty path and what it breaks with a link to fix it, inputs, module and outputs side by side, and the settings that change the numbers.
- Real inputs and outputs for fourteen modules that showed almost nothing
- Estimate money stays in the project currency, link status and element exports filter in the database, and an RFQ without a project currency is refused with a clear code.

Every demo project now opens Design with a confirmed brief, and where the project has a model it shows up as design revision 1, so the editor, revisions and acceptance pages have something real to look at. The editor also explains a missing brief instead of loading forever, and the public demo says plainly that it is read only.

Install or upgrade with `pip install -U openconstructionerp`, or use the installers below.

The macOS build is for Apple Silicon only. On an Intel Mac, install with pip or Docker.

Design gets its own section, from brief and revisions to the estimate, with a full browser editor installed on demand, and every module page opens its data paths.

### Added

- Design section. A design has a brief, revisions with acceptance and a link contract, and its model drives quantities into the estimate, activities into the schedule and packages into procurement. The section stays in the menu, and the light engine works without any download.
- The full browser design editor is installed from the work

Surveyors get a plan editor shared by every survey screen, five site survey workflows run end to end, tenders become one register, and data paths show swimlanes, roles and recent changes.

### Added

- Survey plan editor. Points, lines and parcels are drawn and edited on one canvas with snapping, measuring, layers, a map underlay and printing to scale. Traverses are entered by clicking stations, and the least squares adjustment draws error ellipses with a stated exaggeration.
- Plans for parcels, surfaces,

Subcontract awards carry their terms into the contract, a company can buy once for several projects, survey work gains the geodesy a site surveyor needs, and every module shows where its data comes from and where it goes. An awarded tender hands its payment terms, retention, levies and cash discount to the subcontract, a central buyer splits one package across projects and legal entities, and a Data paths view draws the platform as one connected map with live counts and the firms behind them.

Tendering, contracts and purchase orders answer the questions users raised this week, the CRM tracks deal activities, and a survey family of modules arrives. A tender package shows its contents before it goes out, a bid entered by hand can be priced line by line, contracts print to PDF and keep client and subcontract values apart, and purchase orders can be edited by everyone allowed to change them.

### Added

- Tender package contents. A Contents tab shows every line with quantity, unit, budget rate a

- Semantic search by catalogue, region and category. The cost database and the resource catalogue first narrow the list by region, catalogue, category, type, unit and price, and only then rank the remaining items by meaning. Without a vector store the search falls back to text search.
- Desktop startup screen. When the desktop app cannot start it shows a screen with Copy log, Open log folder and Repair. Repair asks first, clears a stale lock and sets aside a database folder that never started, and deletes n

- Add experimental support for Oracle's [go-oracledb](https://github.com/oracle/go-oracledb) driver with the `oracledb` build tag and `exporter-oracledb` container target, without CGO or Oracle Instant Client.

- Set `CLIENT_INFO` to `oracledb_exporter` on every new database session for both godror and go-ora, including replacement connections, and fail connection initialization if the marker cannot be set. Configure the label or opt out with `metrics.clientInfo` (defaults: `label: oracledb_exporter`, `enabled: true`).
- Add the optional `oracledb_exporter_last_metric_scrape_duration_seconds` metric, reporting how long the last scrape of each individual metric took, per database, so slow queries can be identified

- Add the exporter user's passwd entry to the godror container image, preventing concurrent Oracle Client connection creation from aborting when UID 1000 cannot be resolved.
- Treat `ORA-12541: TNS:no listener` as a temporary connection error so unavailable database listeners honor `connectionBackoff`.
- Enable godror's Oracle session pool whenever a `poolIncrement`, `poolMaxConnections`, or `poolMinConnections` setting is configured, and cap warmup at the configured pool maximum.

Dependency maintenance release: updates .NET 10 servicing dependencies to 10.0.15, refreshes the test framework and polyfills, updates NanoMsgSharp to 1.1.5, and refreshes the Rust interop lockfile. No public API or target-framework changes. All four RaftCs packages are published to GitHub Packages; NuGet.org promotion is running separately through trusted publishing.

NuGet.org promotion 40334670890 authenticated all four GitHub-feed downloads and successfully published them. All four public NuGet packages were subsequently downloaded and their IDs, versions, repository URL, and embedded source commit verified as 0d7d478add8b4059cf7d694dac24f6670db50d5c. RaftCs.Transport.NanoMsg depends on NanoMsgSharp 1.1.4 for every supported target framework.

## What's changed

- Deliver committed commands with their log index and term through `RaftNode.CommittedItems` (#9).
- Bound file-storage disk usage with durable, access-preserving log compaction (#10).
- Add application snapshot creation, delivery to lagging followers, and restoration before replay on restart (#11).
- Preserve snapshot generation, indexed membership, hard state, and rollback guards across compaction and recovery.
- Fail pending snapshot requests when the node stops after a storage f

Terchess v1.1.6 is a stable release. Download the cross-platform Terchess ZIP, extract it, and use run_terchess.bat (Windows), run_terchess.command (macOS), or run_terchess.sh (Linux). On first launch the script installs Python dependencies. One-command installers detect existing Stockfish engines and offer update or side-by-side installation choices; manual ZIP installations require a separate Stockfish setup. Terchess can remember your preferred engine or show the engine selector at startup.
